note: Israel (and the West Bank and Gaza, whose access Israel controls): nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for up to 90 days for tourism, business or study, but since 1 January 2025 must first obtain the ETA-IL electronic travel authorisation; Indians and Sri Lankans may get an e-Visa online (up to 90 days); everyone else needs a visa, and nationals of states hostile to Israel a special permit (taken as a visa). Read from Wikipedia's copy of the Population and Immigration Authority's lists. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Population and Immigration Authority's own ETA-IL portal and the data it serves (each nationality's NEED_PERMIT): every passport held for the ETA-IL is marked as needing no visa but Moldova's, which needs one and was moved to the visa; the territories it marks the same way (Anguilla, Guam, Guadeloupe and the rest) are their states' passports here, which the list already names. The portal gives the e-Visa pilot for Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders resident there; the 90 days stand on Wikipedia's copy.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Israel
sources.said: Nationals of the following countries may enter Israel without a visa for tourist, business or study purposes for up to 90 days, or for culture or sport activities for up to 30 days. From 1 January 2025, they must obtain an electronic travel authorization (ETA-IL) before travelling to Israel. ... sources.title: Population and Immigration Authority, ETA-IL portal home (rendered)
sources.said: As of January 1st, 2025, travelers to Israel must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey. If you are a citizen of a visa-exempt country, answer a few questions to see if you're eligible for an ETA-IL. ... eVisa-B2 The pilot program for the new e-visa system is now up and running. Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders residing in India and Sri Lanka can now apply for a B2 visa directly on the official website.
